gloss: to nearly die; to be on the verge of death

definitions.gloss: to nearly die; to be on the verge of death; to be about to die
definitions.explanation: To come very close to dying, either literally from illness or accident, or hyperbolically to express extreme discomfort or distress.

examples.japanese: {交通事故|こうつうじこ}で{死|し}にかけた。
examples.english: I nearly died in a traffic accident.

examples.japanese: {暑|あつ}さで{死|し}にかけている。
{子供|こども}のころ{川|かわ}で{溺|おぼ}れて{死|し}にかけた{経験|けいけん}がある。
examples.english: As a child, I once nearly drowned to death in a river.

notes:
A compound verb formed from {死|し}ぬ (to die) + かける (to be about to; to be on the verge of). The auxiliary verb 〜かける attaches to the masu-stem of verbs to express that an action has started but not completed, or is about to happen. Common in both serious and exaggerated/humorous contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {死|し}にかけた{経験|けいけん}: a near-death experience
- {死|し}にかけている: to be on the verge of death; to be dying (literal or hyperbolic)
- {暑|あつ}さで{死|し}にかける: to nearly die from the heat

COMMON PATTERNS:
The 〜かける pattern is productive and can attach to many verbs to mean "about to" or "half-": {食|た}べかける (to start eating), {読|よ}みかける (to start reading), {壊|こわ}れかける (to be about to break).

USAGE:
This is an ichidan verb. Past: {死|し}にかけた. Te-form: {死|し}にかけて. Progressive: {死|し}にかけている.

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {死|し}にかけていませんでした
